title.narrative: Tamil Nadu and Puducherry Coastal Disaster Risk Reduction Project

description.narrative: Increasing the resilience of coastal communities in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, to a range of hydro-meteorological and geophysical hazards along with improving project implementing entities capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency.

The objective of the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry Coastal Disaster Risk Reduction Project for India is increasing the resilience of coastal communities in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, to a range of hydrometeorological and geophysical hazards along with improving project implementation entities? capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency. The project has five components. The first component is vulnerability reduction. The objective of this component is to reduce the vulnerability of coastal communities through infrastructure such as permanent houses, evacuation shelters and routes, and resilient electrical networks. It has following three sub-components: (i) resilient housing; (ii) evacuation shelters, routes and early warning systems; and (iii) cyclone resilient electrical network. The second component is sustainable fisheries. The objective of this component is to address gaps in the context of a long term vision for the fisheries sector. The component aims at upgrading infrastructure, developing an approach for co-management of fisheries and addressing safety at sea. This component has following two sub-components: (a) fishing infrastructure; and (b) Second Fisheries Management for Sustainable Livelihood (FIMSUL II). The third component is capacity building in disaster risk management. This component will focus on strengthening the capacity of government institutions, civil society, the school education system and coastal communities through following four sub-components: (i) strengthening of state disaster management authority; (ii) Community Based Disaster Risk Management Program (CBDRM); (iii) curriculum development on disaster risk reduction for schools and training institutions; and (iv) completing preparation of the Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) plan for Tamil Nadu, completing erection of High Tide Line (HTL) pillars across all 13 coastal districts and stake holder training on coastal zone management. The fourth component is implementation support. This will include incremental operating costs, that of operating the Project Management Unit (PMU) and respective Project Implementation Units (PIUs) in the line departments. In addition, the component will include consultancies required for the preparation and supervision of specific activities, trainings, exposure visits and knowledge exchange programs. The fifth component is contingent emergency financing. This component will draw resources from the unallocated expenditure category and or allow the government of Tamil Nadu and or Puducherry to request the Bank to re-categorize and reallocate financing from other project components to partially cover emergency response and recovery costs.

title.narrative: Number of old bridges rehabilitated and reconstructed

comment.narrative: <p>In PY three old bridges were listed for rehabilitated and reconstruction. For the bridges, however though initial design work was taken up, as documented in the AM Aug 2017, the mission was informed the three bridges would be taken up by the PWD. Hence the target was 'Not Achieved'.</p>

title.narrative: Integration of multiple Emergency Operation Centre

comment.narrative: <p>Integration of multiple Emergency Operation Centre was not taken up under this project. The reasons for this included delayon behalf of the Government counterparts in finalising their respective proposals and in sharing the same with the Bank. THus the target is 'Not Achieved'</p>

title.narrative: Establishment of a Centre for Disaster Management (TAMIL NADU)

comment.narrative: <p>The setting up of a Centre for Disaster Management was part of the project, however, the project was not able to establish this center. The reasons for this included delay on behalf of the Government counterparts in finalising their respective proposals and in sharing the same with the Bank. Additionally, the GoTN found it difficult to get a suitable, well located piece of land, this too delayed the activity. Thus the target is 'Not Achieved'</p>

title.narrative: Enhanced performance of livelihood opportunities from fisheries with increased safety at sea

comment.narrative:
<ol>
 <li>Safety at Sea: The project built the country’s first-of-its-kind wireless communication early warning system for fishers, equipping 18,555 fishers with Very High Frequency (VHF) sets achieving 371% of its original target of 5,000 fishers.  Thus, 'achieved' its target of fishers with wireless communication facilities. Seven new 100m VHF communication towers have been constructed, additionally six BSNL towers and two Police department towers have been hired and fifteen control rooms established for continuous communication throughout the coast of Tamil Nadu</li>
 <li>Fisheries co-management: For the first time in the countryhas such a large co-management exercise been formally undertaken by any project or state government. The project established '4' Regional level co-management committees and involved them in FMPs as against the target of '4' in the PAD, thus 'achieved' the target. Additionally the project established a total of 619 co-management committee’s across the two project states. In TN the project established 35 Fishing Harbour Management Committees across 8 districts, 541 fishery co-management committees at village level, 13 at districts, 4 at regional and 1 at state level and in PY it established 25 fishery co-management committees at village level</li>
 <li>Fisheries infrastructure: The project supported the building and modernization of a total of39 fisheries infrastructure, instead of the originally planned 19, and providing access to 49 villages to fishing related restored linkages/infrastructure, higher than the original target of 46. Thus at 106% achievement it 'achieved' its target. In TN the project built 2 fish landing centers, 3 fishing harbors, 2 river bar mouths, 1 tube ice plant, 1 stability of coastal inlet, and in PY  modernized 2 fishing harbors, built 23 work shelters, built 1 new fish market and modernized 4 existing fish markets</li>
</ol>

title.narrative: Increased community resilience and preparedness in coastal areas

comment.narrative:
<ol>
 <li>The project constructed 121 MPCSs and 41 KM evacuation routes in TN, providing shelter to the poor households, especially in vulnerable locations and improved access to the MPCS achieving 100% of its shelter target, and achieving 93% of its original and 100% of its revised (Restructuring June 30, 2020) evacuation route target. Thus it 'achieved' it's target of habitations with access to community managed emergency shelter. Based on the location, catchment area’s population and community needs, three types of multi-purpose shelters were designed to function as Community Halls, Schools, PHCs respectively during regular time and for evacuation during emergency.  Operational Guidelines for the Management and Maintenance of Multi-Purpose Evacuation Shelters were issued by the GoTN as per which a Shelter Management Committee was constituted, for each of the 121 shelters. A bank account was opened, a corpus fund sanctioned by the GoTN was deposited and the interest accrued in the account will be available for basic repairs and maintenance.</li>
 <li>The project constructed 15,534 multi-hazard resilient houses (14,347 in TN and 1,187 in Py) achieving 97% of the initial target of 16,000 and achieving 106% of the revised target of 14,649 (Restructuring June 30, 2020) houses, thus 'achieved' it's target of households with Quality certified multi-hazard resilient houses</li>
 <li>The project set up a comprehensive Early Warning system, “Tamil Nadu State Wide Area Network (TNSWAN)” Ethernet network that can broadcast early warning announcements to towers installed at  450 sites, achieving 102% of the originally planned 439 sites and achieving 100% of its revised target (Restructuring June 30, 2020) of 450. Thus, 'achieved' its target of coastal population covered by the early warning systems. This includes 1 main Disaster Warning Announcement Systems-Central DWAS-C server that is anchored at the Disaster Management Cell in Cheppauk and the backup server in Tirunelveli. Apartfrom these, the 13 district DWAS-D servers located in respective District Collector offices can relay as well as respond to a localsituation. Each tower has a siren installed, and has an audio and visual range of 1 km radius. The last-mile connectivity is via a radio network through VHF sets. Remotely located communities can also be reached by the siren through the amplifiers that have been created. In case the Ethernet network fails, the messages can be transmitted through mobile phone tower networks. The system has been made resilient through the use of solar panels to ensure a continuous supply of charge with battery backup available fortwo days. Besides, the towers can resist wind speeds of up to 250 km/hr.</li>
 <li>The CBDRM program was successfully completed in all aspects in 561 coastal villages in Tamil Nadu, fulfilling 374% of its original target of 150 and 100% its revised target of 560 villages. It trained over 0.4 million individuals  (i) formed Village Disaster Management Committee (VDMCs), (ii) conducted risk and vulnerability assessments and preparation of village disaster risk management plans (VDRMPs), (ii) undertook community mobilisation and capacity building activities such as mock drills, training programs, (iii) formed and trained Village Disaster Mgt Team (VDMT) comprising of five task forces; Early warning; Evacuation; Search and Rescue; Shelter Management and First aid. Women were alsomembers of these, based on their willingness (iv) linked communities to early warning systems and evacuation shelters, and (v) strengthened capacities of first responders. </li>
</ol>

<p> </p>

<ol>
 <li>Underground Electrical Cabling: As of May 15, 2021 the project laid 2022 KM of underground electrical cabling, comprising 1504 KM in Tamil Nadu and 518 KM in Puducherry. The target achieved is 109% of the original target of 1,850 KM reducing significantly the risk to electrical infrastructure in the coastal urbans. Thus it 'achieved' it's target of coastalarea with electrical cabling transferred underground. At time of project closure in June 2020 the total completed cable length was 936 KM within which PY had completed all work, i.e. 518KM and TN had completed only 418 KM. Post project closure TN has proceeded with its own funds to complete the targets.</li>
 <li>Total service connections to be provided in PY were 12,797 which is 100% complete. In TN, of the total 26,407 service connections,  15,252 (58%) have been charged (supply started) and another 4249 (16%) service connections have been connected upto metering point but yet to be charged (supply not started). The reason for this gap is ascribed to Covid related disruptions including lockdown and the May 2021 assembly elections in Tamil Nadu. It is expected that once the ongoing Covid lockdown restrictions are removed rapid progress will be achieved, and all service connections will be charged.</li>
</ol>

comment.narrative: <p>The project built the country’s first-of-its-kind wireless communication early warning system for fishers, equipping 18,555 fishers with Very High Frequency (VHF) sets achieving 371% of its original target of 5,000 fishers. Thus target is 'Achieved'. Seven new 100m VHF communication towers have been constructed, additionally six BSNL towers and two Police department towers have been hired and fifteen control rooms established for continuous communication throughout the coast of Tamil Nadu</p>

<p>Two public buildings were restored, the heritage Mairie Building dated 1871 in  Py and Nehru Market dated 1865 in Karaikal,compared to a target of three (measured by IRI 6). Thus the target is 'Partially Achieved". These were affected by the Tsunami and Cyclone Thane and vulnerable to future hazards, they were important public buildings of cultural and economic value, – the Mairie building located on the touristic promenade of Py  and Nehru Market housed a large number of food and meat vendors. By project closing, the Mairie Building was at 55% rebuilt, the works continued post closing using State funds and as ofJune 30, 2021 it is above 90% completed. In Nehru Market, the project financed 20% additional vending space, improved access, lighting, parking, storage, catering, waste management and toilet facilities. Nehru Market was complete at closing, has been handed over to Karaikal Municipality and  the vending spaces allotment is expected to be complete by October 30, 2021.</p>

<p>the reconstruction and widening of two culverts at Vaithkuppam road and near old Maravadi street in Py that had suffered damage due to severe salinity and were the only means to evacuate in times of distress. These were completed<strong> </strong> in January 2019 (measured by IRI 6). Thus the target was 'Achieved'</p>

It is expected that once Covid lockdown restrictions are removed rapid progress will be achieved, and all service connections will be charged.</p>

title.narrative: Increased institutional capacity for risk mitigation and response at State level

comment.narrative:
<ol>
 <li>Fire Service: The project equipped the Puducherry fire service department with 17 types of modern equipment. The NDRF’s 4th Battalion in Arokkonam and equipment manufacturers trained the Fire Department officials to use the new equipment. </li>
 <li>Comprehensive GIS Platform: TN-SMART - As part of the wider objective to strengthen capacities of government institutions (primarily the SDMA), civil society and communities in disaster management, GoTN in collaboration with the Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early warning Systems (RIMES) developed a decision-support system called the Tamil Nadu System for Multi-hazard potential impact Assessment and emergency Response Tracking (TN-SMART). It was launched on 26 October, 2018.</li>
 <li>Under subcomponent 3.1 Strengthening of State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA), the project was not able to set up of the Centre for Disaste Management in TN and was not able to strengthen the existing Emergency Operation Centre along with a decision support system for Py and Karaikal. The achievement is at 50%, thus the target of Improving Project implementing Entities' capacity to respond promptly and effectively to emergencies was 'partially achieved'</li>
</ol>
